text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programmes that can understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns they have learned. During training, they read enormous amounts of text, such as books, articles and websites. Users can improve results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are good at tasks like summarising, translating and answering questions. However, they have limits: they can make mistakes, invent false information, and their knowledge stops at a certain date. They also cannot truly understand meaning the way people do.
